newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks dragged lower by U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks dragged lower by U.S. data.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower as price fell following U.S. data that showed a surprise jump in the core U.S. inflation rate for March, dealers said.
Swiss stocks fell after Wall Street shed more than 75 points after its opening and dealers expect the market to remain volatile next week.
SMI index of leading shares down 21.8 points at 4,604.8 after high at 4,660.6. All-share SPI down 8.74 points at 2,918.14.
UBS bearer shares ended 20 francs higher at 1,307 on speculative buying. Traders said rumours were again flying that UBS planned an acquisition, or a cooperation deal or a major restructuring step.
The share has also lagged behind other big banks.
Dealers said next week's market was likely to be volatile and sentiment is mainly negative. However, they don't expect a major fall in prices.
"Many investors are rather negative on the market and have reduced positions or are short", one dealer said.
Apart from UBS, most other blue chips closed lower.
Only Holderbank and Alusuisse were firmer. Holderbank, up 19 francs to 1,121, was supported by a buy recommendation from CSFB, one dealer said.
Alussuisse, up nine to 1,181, had been volatile in the recent past and was making up past losses.
Trading volume was 1.83 billion Swiss francs.
Roche fell 90 francs to 12,250 as the market shrugged off a magazine report on rumours that Roche was in talks to acquire and break up Zeneca Group Plc.
Roche said it did not comment on rumors as a matter of principle.
Among the insurers, Swiss Re gave up most of yesterday's gains and ended 15 francs lower at 1,523.
Baloise gained 40 francs to 2,910 on renewed rumors the group could plan a major restructuring.
